title: Year in Review
content:
<p>For the past several years I haven&#39;t felt like doing one of these but this year
seems especially fitting to recap. High‑level, I largely exited crypto, tended
more to my personal spaces (webb.page and blog.webb.page), lost my grandmother,
and more. So it feels weird to say that in this moment I am happy and hopeful
for the future.</p>
<h2>Handshake</h2>
<p>Since late 2019 I&#39;ve been working in the Handshake blockchain space. It actually
fulfills a lifelong dream<a href="https://blog.neuenet.com/post/vision">1</a> so I was incredibly excited and incentivized to
build the infrastructure for the future I want. I learned a LOT. Like how to
write a DNS server! The heavy‑lifting was via a Node.js DNS packet module I
ported to Deno/TypeScript<a href="https://github.com/NetOpWibby/packet">2</a>. Unfortunately, I never figured out how to handle
cert files so I used PowerDNS for my authoritative server instead.</p>
<p>I presented my work‑in‑progress at HandyCon<a href="https://blog.neuenet.com/post/handycon-presentation">3</a>, continued creating mini modules
to support features like NIC pages<a href="https://blog.neuenet.com/post/devlog-010">4</a>, and even got my first customers! One of
them immediately used their domains<a href="https://blog.neuenet.com/post/devlog-012">5</a> and this was easily a top 5 highlight of
my year. Next, I started work on a CDN<a href="https://blog.neuenet.com/post/devlog-013">6</a>. What&#39;s interesting about creating
your own versions of infrastructure we depend on daily is that you realize how
complicated (or not) things are. And, how weird it is that modern literature on
such things is absent.</p>
<p>Four years working in this space…and I decided to quit<a href="https://blog.neuenet.com/post/devlog-014">7</a>. The TL;DR? Grifters
and opportunists seek to subvert the blockchain that was designed for the many,
to financially benefit the few. I cannot and will not support bad faith
proposals or persons supporting them.</p>
<p>The thought of leaving all this work behind hurt a lot and I found myself
wondering what I&#39;d work on next. That&#39;s where Socii comes in.</p>
<h2>Socii</h2>
<p>I was working on Socii<a href="https://socii.network">8</a>, my social network concept, for about a year when I
discovered Handshake. It only made sense to return to (re)developing it. When I
was dusting off the codebase and trying to make sense of it, the U.S. election
concluded and I was in a state of shock about the outcome. The fact that the
entirety of crypto and Big Business was celebrating the win<a href="/2024-11-08-farcaster.txt">9</a> blindsided me. I
was (and still am) disgusted.</p>
<p>In a self‑serving world of sychophants and apathy, it seems we&#39;ve gotta make
what we want to see/use/buy in the world. I&#39;m under no illusions that I&#39;ll get
explosive growth and a billion users on my platform and quite frankly, I don&#39;t
want that. I want <em>customers</em> who are willing to pay for a social network that
empowers them to do more with their online presence whilst providing a curated
private space for them and the people they care to connect with. Building a
sustainable business is actually not that complicated…it&#39;s just the opposite of
what&#39;s celebrated in the market today and quite frankly…fuck the market.</p>
<p>Since the election, hordes of people have fled Twitter<a href="https://pxlnv.com/linklog/similarweb-traffic-bluesky">10</a> and I believe a
subset of them would be delighted to use the spiritual successor<a href="https://social.coop/@netopwibby/113329030542527807">11</a> to Myspace.
We&#39;ll see!</p>
<h2>Professional Life</h2>
<p>I&#39;ve utilized side projects my entire career as a way to better my skills and
have fun at the same time. The main reason is because I have way too many ideas
and I&#39;m hella impatient. Why wait for someone to build what I envision when I
can do it myself (and to my specifications)? Another benefit is simply keeping
your skills sharp because technology advances regularly, even if the tools you
use at work are in stasis.</p>
<p>How many times have you run <code>npm install</code> at work and seen a bunch of messages
in Terminal warning you of deprecated modules?</p>
<p>Certain parts of the company I work for are using parts of the tech stack I use
in my personal life, like Svelte/SvelteKit. I&#39;m stuck using Handlebars and old
build systems. Navigating corporate hierarchy to get onto other teams is an
exercise in frustration. I&#39;ve gotten either no response or laugh reactions to my
questions about such in the company Slack (only for said reactor to rescind when
confronted). Strange how being part of a trillion dollar company is lonelier
than being part of a startup.</p>
<p>Aligning my values with what I work on is extremely important to me. I certainly
have the skills to find work with a company that fits, if not launch my own! To
that end, it is my hope that 2025 will see me working for myself and/or
likeminded individuals/companies. To some extent, this is a privileged
viewpoint and I pride myself on building up to this point. Our purpose in life
is to be in service to others. I have these skills…why hoard them
for myself?</p>
<h2>Family</h2>
<p>It&#39;s wild how death brings people together. My grandmother passed recently<a href="/2024-12-20-my-grandma.txt">12</a>
and I flew to Ohio for her memorial. Prior to this trip I had been estranged (or
pretty close to being estranged) from my immediate family aside from my youngest
sister (who, unfortunately, couldn&#39;t make the trip). My only focus was honoring
my grandmother&#39;s memory. What I learned is that my experience was not unique. A
cousin mentioned feeling frustrated about being kept away from grandma but was
glad to have connected with her the last time they had a conversation with her.
Another cousin regretted missing a graduation that occured a week prior to her
passing. Yet another cousin expressed the unconditional love she gave despite
his life choices that others judged him for.</p>
<p>My mom pulled me aside to recount the last conversation she had with grandma and
how they were able to finally move forward. I told her grandma told me to
forgive my mother and talk to her. These two events happening the same week
before her passing is nuts…very TV‑like. Anyhoo, I enjoyed myself despite the
initial trepidation and sadness. Remembering our grandma with my cousins was
fun. Her love of fur coats and fashion and willingness to always help someone in
need were much talked about topics.</p>
<p>One of my cousins is a music producer now and he credits me for inspiring him,
which was bewildering to me. Apparently, my beat‑making and raps and how I
designed my bedroom as a teen was enough to influence his career path. I largely
stopped making music because it just didn&#39;t fit with having a family at the time
and the internet wasn&#39;t as democratized for music as it is now. I&#39;m excited to
build with him, we&#39;ve got some things cooking.</p>
<p>At my grandma&#39;s memorial, the pastor said we shouldn&#39;t use funerals as the only
time to link up with family. Communicating with family is something that should
be done all the time, on a regular basis. My problem is when people send weird
energy my way. I don&#39;t like that. Don&#39;t be weird or sideways with me. Say things
with your chest.</p>
<h2>My Spaces</h2>
<p>In 2022 and 2023, I wrote approximatly ONE post for the entire year. Why? I&#39;ve
been using Twitter as my (micro‑)blogging platform of choice. When I got
banned<a href="/2023-07-17-twitter.txt">13</a> it was a slap in the face. 15 years on a platform that kicked me off
almost as soon as ownership changed hands. I eventually regained access<a href="/2024-12-16-twitter.txt">14</a> (ha,
our bad, our spam filters are too powerful) but after almost two years of using
other services, why the hell would I go back? In fact, why am I posting all my
good stuff on platforms I don&#39;t own/control?</p>
<p>I&#39;ve been talking about my personalOS concept<a href="/2019-12-02-a-personal-api.txt">15</a> for many years now and have
longed for my homepage to represent that. I&#39;ve recognized that my default of
&quot;things have to be perfect before launching&quot; is stupid so I decided to go ahead
and relaunch webb.page and update things manually vs via an API. It&#39;s lacking
features but who cares? YOU don&#39;t know what they are and even if you can figure
them out…who cares?! Perfection is something corporations should strive for, not
regular degular folks like myself.</p>
<p>My homepage is my canvas. My blog is my notepad. <code>webb.page</code> is my space.</p>
<h2>2026</h2>
<p>My grandma&#39;s last words to me were about forgiveness. Thinking about her life,
she was fearless. If she had a goal, she made a plan and met it. She had a dual
business (barbershop/beauty salon) and bought a house. No degree necessary, just
hard work and dedication. I want to live my life the same way. I&#39;m a self‑taught
designer/developer and have built neat things thus far. But, while I am
generally fearless, I am still held back but a few things: driving and swimming.
I&#39;m going to get my license next year and possibly learn how to swim.</p>
<p>Eveything else is easy‑peasy. Success is merely a matter of time.</p>
<p>🕸️</p>
<hr>
